source_en: Clinic tutoring. Mother expects me by six.
Stayed late to redo an exam.
Library run before it closes.
Back from the clinic volunteer program.
Studying with a classmate. Mother dislikes lateness.
Collecting textbooks before lessons stopped.
Going home. Nowhere else worth going.
Studying in the empty old clinic.
Home. Mother will ask what I learned.
Home from my bakery job. I left school.
Home to my aunt. She raised me.
Skipped tutoring for a film. Mother lets me.
Quit the ward. Becoming a hairdresser.
Back from my post office job.
Out late on purpose. Mother never asks.
Going home to my husband.
Going to sleep. I quit studying.
Collecting my nurse's pension.
Here. Everything is organised by date, in case that helps.
My mother says punctuality reflects character. I will not be late.
The line was longer yesterday. I timed it. This is faster.
I have a test tomorrow. I would like to be efficient.
My sister is waiting. Please, I have done everything correctly.
Why does this take longer every day? I follow every instruction.
I checked everything. I think. I don't remember checking it.
My hands won't stay still. I'm not usually like this.
I can hear my own heartbeat. Is that normal? Is it?
My mother cannot see me like this. She can't.
Something under my skin isn't mine. I shouldn't have said that.
Just tell me if I did something wrong. Please.
Thank you. I'll tell my mother it went well.
See? I told you everything was in order.
I can still make it home before dark. Thank you.
I would like to keep my study schedule with me.
Someone must tell my mother. She will not handle this.
I was going to be a doctor. A good one.
My mother will say I brought this on myself.
Where are you coming from?
The clinic. Anatomy tutoring, then the volunteer ward. Home by six.
The clinic. The volunteer program still runs. Rolling bandages is still practice.
The old clinic building. Mostly empty now. Quieter than home for studying.
The medical institute. I'm in my third year. Surgery, eventually.
Home. I'm an only child, so it's quiet enough to study.
The textile factory canteen. I gave up medicine long ago.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
No. I sleep too little, but from studying. I know the difference.
Headaches. Reading by candle in the power cuts. Not a symptom.
Cold hands. Little sleep. I took my own pulse. It is normal.
Nothing. I haven't opened a textbook in weeks. No eye strain.
No. My mother lets me rest whenever. She says grades don't matter.
I wouldn't know. Blood makes me faint. I can't take a pulse.
The body survives remarkably specific traumas. It's fascinating, honestly.
I don't usually get nervous. I don't know why I'm nervous.
Does medical school account for checkpoint delays? I doubt it.
I notice things about the body I never used to. Studies, probably.
My sister asked if I was scared. Fear isn't useful information.
I keep counting things. I don't know when I started.
